SPHENIC NUMBERS WITH INTEGRAL RECIPROCAL SUM -- ALL EXAMPLES OBTAINED SO FAR
==============================================================================
Each example is a set T of sphenic numbers p*q*r (p<q<r primes) with
    sum_{n in T} 1/n = 1   EXACTLY
(an integral sum over <= 73081 terms is necessarily 1, because H_73081 = 1.5557... < 2).
148 examples are listed (E01-E148); every one was regenerated by sphenic_search.py and verified by
verify_sphenic.py with exact integer / rational arithmetic only (Fraction sum == 1, every element is a
product of exactly 3 distinct primes, p-adic criterion at every prime). No floating point anywhere.

OVERVIEW
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  examples in total            : 148
  with |T| <= 6096             : 97
  with |T| >  6096             : 51
  smallest |T|                 : 5151 terms (E25, seed k=4656, scan attempt 46)
  largest  |T|                 : 6668 terms (E119)
  median   |T|                 : 5933
  group A  E01-E11             : 11 individual runs (default settings or B=6096 / B=73081 runs)
  group B  E12-E148           : 137 solutions of one 400-attempt scan (seed 99, k in [4390,6190))
  lower bound (proved)         : |T| >= 4402, because H_4401 < 1 (H_k = sum of the k smallest reciprocals)
  minimality is NOT claimed; the true minimum is unknown.

  distribution of |T| over all examples:
     5100 <= |T| <  5400 :   7
     5400 <= |T| <  5700 :  35
     5700 <= |T| <  6000 :  40
     6000 <= |T| <  6100 :  16
     6100 <= |T| <  6400 :  32
     6400 <= |T| <  6700 :  18

HOW TO REPRODUCE (run in the repository root; the search is deterministic)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Group A (attempt = repair pass number within that run; default PRNG seed 20260929 unless --seed is given;
defaults are --bound 6096 --kmin 4900 --kmax 5300):
  E01: python3 sphenic_search.py --bound 73081 --kmin 4390 --kmax 6190 --out FILE
  E02: python3 sphenic_search.py --bound 6096 --kmin 4390 --kmax 6190 --out FILE
  E03: python3 sphenic_search.py --out FILE
  E04: python3 sphenic_search.py --seed 1 --out FILE
  E05: python3 sphenic_search.py --seed 2 --out FILE
  E06: python3 sphenic_search.py --seed 3 --out FILE
  E07: python3 sphenic_search.py --seed 4 --out FILE
  E08: python3 sphenic_search.py --seed 5 --out FILE
  E09: python3 sphenic_search.py --seed 6 --out FILE
  E10: python3 sphenic_search.py --seed 7 --out FILE
  E11: python3 sphenic_search.py --seed 8 --out FILE

Group B (E12-E148): one command produces all of them, in the order of increasing attempt number:
  python3 sphenic_search.py --bound 73081 --minimize --tries 400 --kmin 4390 --kmax 6190 --seed 99 --dump-all FILE --out BEST
  FILE then holds, for every set with sum exactly 1, a line '# attempt=A k=K size=S' followed by the
  numbers; BEST receives the smallest one (5151 terms, attempt 46, seed size k = 4656).
  E12 is the first such set (smallest attempt number), E148 the last.
